title: Chicken parmesan
summary: Crispy breaded chicken cutlets topped with tomato sauce, melted mozzarella and Parmesan.
method: Warm 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a saucepan over low heat. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds without browning, then add the passata, oregano and salt. Simmer until slightly thickened.
Slice the chicken breasts horizontally into two cutlets and pat dry. Coat each in flour, then beaten eggs, then panko mixed with parmesan, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Heat the remaining oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Fry the cutlets in batches for 3–4 minutes per side until golden, then lay them in a baking dish.
Spoon sauce over each cutlet, leaving crisp edges showing, and scatter with mozzarella. Bake at 200°C until the cheese bubbles and the chicken reaches 74°C in the centre. Rest for 3 minutes.

stages.title: Prepare the tomato sauce
steps: Warm 1 tbsp oil in a saucepan and gently cook minced garlic for 30 seconds without browning.
Add passata and oregano, season with salt and simmer uncovered until slightly thickened.

stages.title: Bread the chicken
steps: Slice each breast horizontally into two thin cutlets and pat dry.
Set out flour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs mixed with parmesan in separate dishes; coat each cutlet in that order, pressing crumbs on firmly.

stages.title: Brown the cutlets
steps: Heat remaining oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Fry cutlets in batches for 3–4 minutes per side until golden; transfer to a baking dish without stacking.

stages.title: Bake and serve
steps: Spoon a little sauce over each cutlet, leaving some crisp edges visible, and scatter with mozzarella.
Bake at 200°C until the cheese bubbles and chicken reaches 74°C in the centre; rest for 3 minutes before serving.

tips: Keep some breadcrumbs uncovered by sauce so the crust stays crisp.
variations: Serve over spaghetti or with a green salad.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat in the oven until piping hot.

title: Beef stroganoff
summary: Tender strips of beef and mushrooms coated in a silky mustard and sour cream sauce.
method: Pat the beef dry and season with salt. Sear in batches in the oil in a wide pan over high heat, about 1 minute per side until browned, then set aside.
Reduce to medium, melt the butter and soften the sliced onion for 4 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook until their moisture evaporates and the edges are golden. Stir in the paprika and flour for 1 minute.
Stir in the stock, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer until lightly thickened. Reduce to low and fold in the mustard and sour cream without boiling.
Cook the egg noodles in salted water until tender, then drain.
Return the beef and its juices to the sauce for 1–2 minutes, just until heated through. Serve over the noodles.

stages.title: Prepare and sear the beef
steps: Pat beef dry and season with salt and pepper; heat oil in a wide pan until hot.
Sear in small batches for about 1 minute per side so it browns rather than steams; transfer to a plate.

stages.title: Build the mushroom base
steps: Reduce heat to medium, melt butter and soften sliced onion for 4 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook until their moisture evaporates and edges turn golden; stir in paprika and flour for 1 minute.

stages.title: Make the sauce
steps: Gradually stir in stock, scraping browned bits from the pan; simmer until lightly thickened.
Reduce heat to low and fold in mustard and sour cream without allowing the sauce to boil.

stages.title: Finish with noodles
steps: Cook egg noodles in salted water until tender and drain.
Return beef and its juices to the warm sauce for 1–2 minutes, just until heated through, then serve immediately over noodles.

tips: Do not boil after adding sour cream or it may split.
variations: Use chicken thigh strips instead of beef, cooking fully before serving.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat gently and do not boil.

title: Teriyaki salmon bowls
summary: Glazed salmon over fluffy rice with sweet-savoury teriyaki sauce, vegetables and sesame.
method: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook on medium heat as directed on the packet. Rest covered off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff.
Whisk the soy sauce, mirin, honey, rice vinegar, ginger and grated garlic together for the glaze.
Slice the cucumber and shred the carrots, then keep them chilled until serving.
Sear the patted-dry salmon skin-side down in a lightly oiled nonstick pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes. Turn and cook until opaque and flaking.
Add the glaze and bubble briefly until glossy and the salmon is cooked through.
Divide the rice between bowls, add the cucumber and carrots, then top with salmon, glaze and sesame seeds.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook over medium heat with the amount of water directed on the packet.
Keep covered off the heat for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

stages.title: Mix the glaze and vegetables
steps: Whisk soy sauce, mirin, honey, vinegar, ginger and grated garlic together.
Slice cucumber and shred carrots; keep them chilled until serving.

stages.title: Cook and glaze the salmon
steps: Pat salmon dry and sear skin-side down in a lightly oiled nonstick pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes.
Turn, cook until the thickest part is opaque and flakes easily, then add the glaze and bubble briefly until glossy; ensure fish is cooked through.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Divide rice between bowls and add cucumber and carrots.
Top with salmon, spoon over reduced glaze and finish with sesame seeds.

tips: Add the glaze only near the end so the honey does not burn.
variations: Replace salmon with firm tofu; brown the tofu well before glazing.
storage: Refrigerate cooked fish and rice separately up to 2 days; chill rice promptly.

title: Vegetable pad Thai
summary: Rice noodles stir-fried with vegetables, egg, tamarind and peanuts for a sweet, tangy finish.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fish sauce or soy sauce
method: Soak the rice noodles in warm water until flexible but still firm, then drain. Stir the tamarind, fish or soy sauce and brown sugar together until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the cubed, pressed tofu until golden on several sides, then push it to the edge.
Crack the eggs into the clear part of the pan and scramble until just set.
Add the noodles, julienned carrots and sauce. Toss until the noodles soften and absorb the sauce, adding a splash of water if needed.
Fold in the bean sprouts and sliced spring onions for the final minute so they stay crunchy.
Serve topped with crushed peanuts and lime wedges for squeezing.

stages.title: Soak noodles and mix sauce
steps: Soak rice noodles in warm water until flexible but still firm, following packet guidance; drain well.
Stir tamarind, fish sauce or soy sauce and sugar together until the sugar dissolves.

stages.title: Brown the tofu
steps: Press tofu dry, cube it and heat oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry tofu until golden on several sides, then move it to the edge of the pan.

stages.title: Cook eggs and noodles
steps: Crack eggs into the clear part of the pan and scramble until just set.
Add noodles, julienned carrots and sauce; toss constantly, adding a splash of water if needed, until noodles soften and absorb the sauce.

stages.title: Finish quickly
steps: Fold in bean sprouts and sliced spring onions for the final minute so they retain crunch.
Serve with crushed peanuts and lime wedges for squeezing.

tips: Prepare every ingredient before heating the wok; the stir-fry moves quickly.
variations: Use prawns instead of tofu, cooking them until opaque.
storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days; reheat thoroughly, adding a little water.

title: Lamb kofta with yoghurt
summary: Juicy spiced lamb kofta served with cooling garlic yoghurt, herbs and warm flatbread.
method: Grate the onion and squeeze out the liquid. Mix with the lamb mince, garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, parsley and 1 tsp salt.
Shape the mixture into 8 short oval patties, by hand or around skewers.
Mix the Greek yoghurt with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice and a pinch of salt. Fold in half the diced cucumber.
Heat the olive oil in a griddle or frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the kofta, turning, for about 10 minutes, until browned all over and cooked through to 71°C.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan until pliable. Serve the kofta with the yoghurt, remaining cucumber, extra parsley and lemon wedges.

stages.title: Mix and shape the kofta
steps: Grate onion and squeeze out excess liquid; combine with lamb, minced garlic, spices, parsley and 1 tsp salt.
Mix just until evenly combined and shape into 8 short oval patties around skewers or by hand.

stages.title: Prepare the yoghurt sauce
steps: Mix yoghurt with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice and a pinch of salt.
Dice cucumber and fold half into the yoghurt, keeping the remainder for serving.

stages.title: Cook the kofta
steps: Heat a griddle or frying pan with oil over medium-high heat.
Cook kofta, turning every few minutes, until browned on all sides and cooked through to 71°C in the centre.

stages.title: Serve with flatbread
steps: Warm flatbreads briefly in a dry pan until pliable.
Serve kofta with yoghurt, cucumber, extra parsley and lemon wedges.

tips: Do not overmix the lamb or the kofta can become dense.
variations: Use beef mince or a beef-lamb mixture.
storage: Refrigerate cooked kofta up to 3 days; keep yoghurt sauce separately.

title: Classic fish tacos
summary: Flaky seasoned fish tucked into tortillas with crunchy slaw and a tangy lime dressing.
method: Shred the red cabbage and slice the red onion. Toss with the juice of one lime, a pinch of salt and the coriander, then leave to stand.
Pat the fish dry, cut into broad strips and coat with the paprika, cumin, olive oil and salt.
Cook the fish in a nonstick pan over high heat for 3–4 minutes per side, until opaque and flaking easily.
Mash the avocado with a squeeze of lime and salt. Stir the Greek yoghurt with the remaining lime juice and a tablespoon of water until spoonable.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan over medium heat until flexible. Fill with fish, slaw, avocado and lime yoghurt, and serve straight away.

stages.title: Make the slaw
steps: Finely shred cabbage and thinly slice red onion.
Toss with juice from one lime, a pinch of salt and a little coriander; let stand while preparing fish.

stages.title: Season and cook the fish
steps: Pat fish dry, cut into broad strips and coat with paprika, cumin, salt and olive oil.
Cook in a hot nonstick pan for 3–4 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until opaque and easily flaked.

stages.title: Prepare toppings
steps: Mash avocado with a squeeze of lime and salt.
Stir yoghurt with remaining lime juice and a tablespoon of water until spoonable.

stages.title: Warm and assemble
steps: Warm tortillas one at a time in a dry pan until flexible.
Fill with fish, cabbage slaw, avocado and lime yoghurt; serve immediately.

tips: Dry the fish well before seasoning to encourage browning.
variations: Replace fish with prawns, cooking until opaque and firm.
storage: Refrigerate cooked fish up to 2 days; store slaw and sauces separately.

title: Chicken fajitas
summary: Sizzling chicken strips with peppers and onions, smoky spices and warm flour tortillas.
method: Slice the chicken, peppers and red onion into thin strips. Toss the chicken with half the olive oil, paprika, cumin, oregano, salt and lime zest.
Heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Cook the peppers and onion in batches until lightly charred but still with some bite.
Move the vegetables to a plate. Cook the chicken in a single layer over high heat, turning, until golden and 74°C in the thickest pieces.
Return the vegetables to the pan and squeeze over the lime juice.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or in foil in the oven. Serve the filling with sour cream and sliced avocado.

stages.title: Slice and season
steps: Cut chicken into even thin strips and slice peppers and onion to a similar thickness.
Toss chicken with half the oil, spices, salt and lime zest; keep raw chicken separate from vegetables.

stages.title: Cook the vegetables
steps: Heat a large frying pan until hot, add remaining oil and cook peppers and onion in batches.
Let them char lightly before stirring so they develop colour while retaining some bite.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Transfer vegetables to a plate and add chicken in a single layer.
Cook, turning, until golden and the thickest pieces reach 74°C; return vegetables and squeeze over lime juice.

stages.title: Serve hot
steps: Warm tortillas in a dry pan or wrapped in foil in the oven.
Serve the sizzling filling with sour cream and sliced avocado.

tips: Use a large pan and avoid crowding to prevent steaming.
variations: Replace chicken with sliced portobello mushrooms for a vegetarian option.
storage: Refrigerate filling up to 3 days; store tortillas and toppings separately.

title: Prawn linguine with chilli
summary: Linguine tossed with juicy prawns, garlic, chilli, olive oil and a bright squeeze of lemon.
method: Boil the linguine in salted water until just short of al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water, then drain. Thinly slice the garlic and chilli.
Pat the prawns dry. Sear them in 1 tbsp oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat until pink and opaque, then remove.
Lower to medium-low heat and add the remaining oil, garlic and chilli. Cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes and cook until softened. Pour in the wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Toss in the pasta with a splash of reserved water until the sauce turns glossy and coats the strands.
Return the prawns briefly. Finish with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice and the parsley, then serve.

stages.title: Prepare pasta and aromatics
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook linguine until just short of al dente.
Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining; thinly slice garlic and chilli.

stages.title: Cook the prawns
steps: Pat prawns dry and heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear prawns briefly on both sides until pink and opaque; remove promptly to avoid toughness.

stages.title: Build the sauce
steps: Lower heat and add remaining oil, garlic and chilli; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add halved tomatoes and cook until they soften, then pour in wine and simmer until reduced by half.

stages.title: Combine and finish
steps: Add pasta and a splash of reserved water, tossing until a glossy sauce coats the strands.
Return prawns briefly, add lemon zest, parsley and a squeeze of juice, and serve.

tips: Prawns cook quickly; remove them as soon as they turn opaque.
variations: Use finely diced courgette instead of tomatoes.
storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days; reheat gently until hot.

title: Roast chicken with lemon
summary: Golden roast chicken with crisp skin, juicy meat, lemon, garlic and fragrant herbs.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Pat the chicken dry, rub with olive oil, thyme, salt and pepper, then put the halved lemon and garlic in the cavity.
Spread the quartered onions in a roasting tray and sit the chicken on top, breast-side up. Pour the stock around the chicken, not over it.
Roast for 75–90 minutes, until the thickest part of the thigh reaches 74°C and the skin is golden.
Rest the chicken under loose foil for 15 minutes, then carve and spoon over the strained roasting juices.

stages.title: Prepare the chicken
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C conventional (180°C fan); pat chicken dry inside and out.
Rub skin with oil, thyme, salt and pepper; place halved lemon and garlic inside the cavity without packing tightly.

stages.title: Set up the roasting tray
steps: Quarter onions and spread them in a roasting tray, then place chicken breast-side up on top.
Pour stock around, not over, the chicken so the skin stays dry.

stages.title: Roast and check
steps: Roast for approximately 75–90 minutes, basting only if the pan becomes dry.
Check the thickest part of the thigh without touching bone reaches 74°C; continue roasting if needed.

stages.title: Rest and carve
steps: Transfer chicken to a board, loosely tent with foil and rest for 15 minutes.
Carve into portions and spoon over strained roasting juices.

tips: A thermometer is more reliable than judging doneness by colour.
variations: Add carrots and potatoes around the chicken for a one-pan meal.
storage: Refrigerate carved chicken up to 3 days; freeze up to 3 months.

title: Beef and broccoli stir-fry
summary: Tender beef and crisp broccoli coated in a glossy ginger, garlic and soy sauce.
method: Cook the rice on low heat to the packet instructions until tender, and keep it covered.
Whisk the soy sauce, oyster sauce, cornflour, sesame oil and water until smooth. Thinly slice the beef rump across the grain.
Blanch the broccoli florets in boiling water on high heat for 90 seconds, then drain well.
Heat the neutral oil in a wok over high heat until very hot. Sear the beef in batches for 1–2 minutes until browned but still tender, then set aside.
Add the garlic and ginger for 20 seconds, then the broccoli and sauce. Simmer until glossy and thickened, return the beef briefly and serve over the rice.

stages.title: Prepare rice and sauce
steps: Cook rice according to packet instructions and keep covered.
Whisk soy sauce, oyster sauce, cornflour, sesame oil and water until smooth; slice beef thinly across the grain.

stages.title: Blanch broccoli
steps: Cut broccoli into small florets and blanch in boiling water for 90 seconds.
Drain thoroughly so it does not dilute the stir-fry sauce.

stages.title: Sear beef
steps: Heat a wok or wide pan until very hot and add neutral oil.
Sear beef in batches for 1–2 minutes, stirring minimally at first; remove while still tender.

stages.title: Finish the stir-fry
steps: Add garlic and ginger for 20 seconds, then broccoli and sauce.
Simmer while stirring until glossy and thickened; return beef briefly and serve over rice.

tips: Slicing across the grain keeps beef tender.
variations: Replace beef with sliced chicken thigh, cooking fully before adding sauce.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; cool rice promptly and reheat thoroughly.

title: Chickpea and spinach curry
summary: Chickpeas and spinach simmered in a warming tomato curry with ginger and aromatic spices.
method: Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Soften the chopped onion until golden at the edges, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the curry powder and cumin for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomatoes and simmer until thickened and the oil starts to separate.
Add the drained chickpeas, coconut milk and 100 ml water. Simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Stir in the spinach by handfuls until wilted, then season with salt and lemon juice. Simmer until the sauce coats the chickpeas.
Rest off the heat for a few minutes, then serve with basmati rice or warm flatbread.

stages.title: Cook the aromatics
steps: Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat and soften finely chopped onion until golden at the edges.
Add garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then stir in curry powder and cumin for 30 seconds to bloom the spices.

stages.title: Build the curry
steps: Add chopped tomatoes and simmer until thickened and the oil begins to separate slightly.
Drain and rinse chickpeas, add with coconut milk and 100 ml water, then simmer gently for 10 minutes.

stages.title: Wilt spinach and season
steps: Add spinach by handfuls, stirring until each batch wilts.
Season with salt and lemon juice; simmer briefly until the sauce coats the chickpeas.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Rest the curry off the heat for a few minutes to let flavours settle.
Serve with basmati rice or warm flatbread.

tips: Rinse canned chickpeas to remove excess brine.
variations: Add diced sweet potato early in the simmer and cook until tender.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; freeze up to 3 months.

title: Creamy mushroom pasta
summary: Silky pasta coated in a savoury mushroom cream sauce with garlic and Parmesan.
method: Boil the fettuccine in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve 200 ml of the cooking water, then drain.
Slice the mushrooms and cook in the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat, in batches, until golden and the moisture has evaporated.
Add the butter and shallot and cook until softened. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Pour in the cream and simmer gently. Stir in the parmesan and a little pasta water until smooth, without boiling hard.
Toss the pasta through the sauce until evenly coated, loosening with more pasta water if needed.
Finish with the parsley, lemon juice and black pepper.

stages.title: Cook pasta
steps: Boil fettuccine in well-salted water until al dente.
Reserve 200 ml cooking water before draining.

stages.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps: Slice mushrooms and cook in a large pan with oil over medium-high heat in batches, until golden brown.
Let their moisture evaporate before stirring often; add butter and shallot once browned.

stages.title: Make the cream sauce
steps: Add minced garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in cream and simmer gently.
Stir in grated parmesan and a little pasta water until smooth; avoid a hard boil.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Add pasta and toss vigorously until evenly coated, loosening with more pasta water as needed.
Finish with parsley, lemon juice and black pepper.

tips: Browning mushrooms well creates the savoury base.
variations: Add cooked shredded chicken for a heartier meal.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat gently with a splash of water.

title: Eggplant parmigiana
summary: Soft aubergine layered with rich tomato sauce, basil, mozzarella and Parmesan, baked until bubbling.
method: Slice the eggplants lengthwise into 1 cm slices, salt them and rest for 10 minutes. Pat dry and brush both sides with olive oil.
Roast the slices in a single layer at 220°C, in batches, until soft and golden, turning halfway.
Meanwhile, cook the garlic in a little oil in a pan over medium heat for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the passata and simmer until slightly thickened, then stir in the basil.
Layer sauce, eggplant, mozzarella and parmesan in a baking dish, finishing with cheese.
Bake at 190°C until bubbling and golden, then rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

stages.title: Prepare eggplant
steps: Slice eggplants lengthwise into 1 cm slices, sprinkle lightly with salt and rest for 10 minutes.
Pat dry and brush both sides lightly with olive oil.

stages.title: Roast the slices
steps: Arrange eggplant in a single layer on baking trays and roast at 220°C until soft and golden, turning halfway.
Work in batches if needed to avoid steaming.

stages.title: Make the sauce
steps: While eggplant roasts, cook minced garlic in a little oil over medium heat for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add passata, simmer until slightly thickened and stir in torn basil.

stages.title: Layer and bake
steps: Spread a thin layer of sauce in a baking dish, then alternate eggplant, sauce, mozzarella and parmesan.
Finish with cheese and bake at 190°C until bubbling and golden; rest 10 minutes before slicing.

tips: Roasting instead of frying reduces oil while keeping flavour.
variations: Add a layer of sautéed spinach between eggplant slices.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; freeze individual portions up to 2 months.

title: Chicken noodle soup
summary: Comforting chicken broth filled with tender chicken, vegetables and soft noodles.
method: Dice the onion, carrots and celery. Cook in the olive oil in a soup pot over medium heat for about 8 minutes until softened, adding the garlic for the last 30 seconds.
Pour in the stock, add the bay leaf and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the chicken thighs and poach for 15–20 minutes, until cooked through (74°C).
Shred the chicken with two forks and return it to the pot. Add the egg noodles and simmer until tender, following the packet.
Remove the bay leaf and season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Serve hot, scattered with parsley.

stages.title: Soften vegetables
steps: Dice onion, carrots and celery into small even pieces.
Heat oil in a soup pot and cook vegetables over medium heat until softened, then add garlic for 30 seconds.

stages.title: Poach chicken
steps: Pour in stock, add bay leaf and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add chicken thighs and poach until cooked through to 74°C, around 15–20 minutes depending on thickness.

stages.title: Shred and cook noodles
steps: Lift chicken onto a board, shred with two forks and return to the pot.
Add noodles and simmer according to packet instructions until tender.

stages.title: Finish soup
steps: Remove bay leaf, season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Scatter parsley over each bowl and serve hot.

tips: Keep stock at a gentle simmer for tender chicken.
variations: Use cooked rice instead of noodles, adding it at the end.
storage: Refrigerate soup up to 3 days; store noodles separately to prevent sogginess.

title: Spinach and ricotta cannelloni
summary: Pasta tubes stuffed with creamy spinach and ricotta, baked in tomato sauce and melted cheese.
method: Wilt the spinach in a pan over medium heat until soft. Cool, squeeze dry, chop finely and mix with ricotta, egg, half the parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add passata and a splash of water, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Spread a thin layer of sauce in a baking dish. Pipe the filling into the dry cannelloni tubes and arrange them in a single layer.
Cover with the remaining sauce, then top with mozzarella and the remaining parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 10–15 minutes more until the pasta is tender and bubbling.

stages.title: Make the filling
steps: Wilt spinach in a pan, cool slightly and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Chop finely and mix with ricotta, egg, half the parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper.

stages.title: Prepare the tomato sauce
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and cook garlic for about 30 seconds until fragrant, without browning.
Add passata with a splash of water and simmer for 5 minutes; spread a thin layer in a baking dish.

stages.title: Fill and arrange
steps: Spoon ricotta filling into a piping bag or sturdy food bag with the corner snipped.
Pipe into dry cannelloni tubes and arrange in a single layer over sauce.

stages.title: Bake until tender
steps: Cover tubes completely with remaining sauce and sprinkle mozzarella and parmesan over the top.
Cover with foil and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes; uncover and bake 10–15 minutes until pasta is tender and bubbling.

tips: Keep the pasta fully covered in sauce so it cooks evenly.
variations: Replace spinach with finely chopped cooked silverbeet.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freeze baked portions up to 2 months.

title: Honey soy chicken thighs
summary: Juicy chicken thighs glazed with sticky honey, soy, garlic and ginger.
method: Whisk the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, garlic and ginger. Set a little aside in a clean bowl for finishing.
Pat the chicken dry. Heat the oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat and brown the thighs 3–4 minutes per side.
Pour the glaze around the chicken and roast at 190°C, turning once, until the chicken reaches 74°C.
If the juices are thin, stir the cornflour with a tablespoon of cold water into them to thicken.
Cook the rice to packet directions while the chicken roasts.
Slice the chicken and serve over the rice with the pan juices and sliced spring onions.

stages.title: Mix the glaze
steps: Whisk soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, minced garlic and ginger together.
Reserve a small amount in a clean bowl for finishing; do not reuse sauce that has touched raw chicken unless boiled.

stages.title: Brown chicken
steps: Pat thighs dry and heat oil in an oven-safe frying pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken for 3–4 minutes per side, working in batches if necessary.

stages.title: Roast and glaze
steps: Pour glaze around chicken and transfer to a 190°C oven.
Roast until chicken reaches 74°C, turning once; thicken pan juices with cornflour mixed into a tablespoon of cold water if needed.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Cook rice according to packet directions while chicken finishes.
Slice chicken and serve over rice with spooned-over glaze and sliced spring onions.

tips: Watch the glaze near the end because honey can burn.
variations: Add chilli flakes or sesame seeds before serving.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freeze chicken up to 2 months.

title: Turkey meatballs in tomato sauce
summary: Tender turkey meatballs simmered in a herby tomato sauce, ideal with pasta or crusty bread.
method: Combine the turkey mince, egg, breadcrumbs, parmesan, one minced garlic clove, parsley and a pinch of salt. Shape into 16 balls with damp hands.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Brown the meatballs for about 5 minutes until golden, then set aside.
In the same pan, soften the onion and remaining garlic for about 5 minutes. Add the passata and 100 ml water.
Return the meatballs, cover loosely and simmer for 15–20 minutes until cooked through to 74°C.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water until al dente, reserving a little pasta water. Toss with the sauce, top with meatballs and extra parmesan.

stages.title: Mix and shape meatballs
steps: Combine turkey mince, egg, breadcrumbs, parmesan, one minced garlic clove, parsley and a pinch of salt.
Mix gently and shape into 16 equal balls with damp hands; avoid packing too tightly.

stages.title: Brown the meatballs
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Brown meatballs on several sides until golden, about 5 minutes, without fully cooking them; remove to a plate.

stages.title: Simmer in sauce
steps: Soften chopped onion and remaining garlic in the same pan for about 5 minutes until soft and translucent, then add passata and 100 ml water.
Return meatballs, cover loosely and simmer until cooked through to 74°C, about 15–20 minutes.

stages.title: Cook pasta and serve
steps: Boil spaghetti until al dente and reserve a little pasta water.
Toss with tomato sauce, top with meatballs and finish with extra parmesan.

tips: Turkey mince is lean, so gentle mixing prevents tough meatballs.
variations: Use pork mince instead, cooking thoroughly.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freeze meatballs in sauce up to 3 months.

title: Beef bibimbap
summary: Rice topped with seasoned beef, colourful vegetables, a fried egg and spicy gochujang sauce.
method: Cook the rice following the packet directions and keep it covered. Mix the soy sauce, sesame oil and brown sugar through the beef mince.
Julienne the carrots and courgette. Wilt the spinach in a pan over medium heat until just soft, then squeeze dry.
Cook the carrots and courgette separately in the neutral oil over medium heat for 2–3 minutes each, until just tender.
Brown the beef in a hot pan over high heat, breaking up lumps, until cooked through. Fry the eggs until the whites are set.
Divide the rice among four bowls and arrange the beef and vegetables on top. Add the eggs, sesame seeds and gochujang, then mix before eating.

stages.title: Cook rice and season beef
steps: Rinse rice and cook according to packet directions; keep covered until serving.
Mix soy sauce, sesame oil and sugar in a bowl, then stir into beef mince.

stages.title: Prepare vegetables
steps: Julienne carrots and courgette; wilt spinach briefly in a pan over medium heat and squeeze dry.
Cook each vegetable separately in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes so colours and textures remain distinct.

stages.title: Cook beef and eggs
steps: Brown seasoned beef in a hot pan, breaking up lumps, until thoroughly cooked.
Fry eggs to your preferred doneness; cook yolks fully if serving someone at higher risk from undercooked eggs.

stages.title: Assemble bowls
steps: Divide rice among four bowls and arrange beef and vegetables in separate sections.
Top with eggs, sesame seeds and a small spoonful of gochujang; mix before eating.

tips: Keep toppings separate until serving for the classic presentation.
variations: Use tofu instead of beef and season it with the same sauce.
storage: Refrigerate cooked components up to 3 days; store eggs separately and chill rice promptly.

title: Baked macaroni and cheese
summary: Tender macaroni baked in a rich cheese sauce beneath a crisp, golden topping.
method: Boil the macaroni in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet directions, then drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute without browning.
Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Off the heat, stir in the Dijon mustard, grated cheddar and gruyere.
Fold the macaroni through the sauce, tip into a lightly buttered baking dish and scatter over the panko mixed with the parmesan.
Bake at 190°C until bubbling at the edges and golden on top, then rest for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Cook pasta
steps: Boil macaroni in salted water for 2 minutes less than packet directions.
Drain well; it will finish cooking in the oven.

stages.title: Make the cheese sauce
steps: Melt butter over medium heat, whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute without browning.
Add milk gradually while whisking and simmer until thick enough to coat a spoon; remove from heat and stir in mustard and grated cheeses.

stages.title: Assemble the bake
steps: Fold macaroni through the cheese sauce and pour into a lightly buttered baking dish.
Mix panko with parmesan and scatter evenly over the surface.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Bake at 190°C until bubbling around the edges and golden on top.
Rest 5 minutes before serving so the sauce settles slightly.

tips: Remove sauce from heat before adding cheese to reduce graininess.
variations: Fold in steamed broccoli or cooked bacon before baking.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat covered with a splash of milk.

title: Lentil shepherd's pie
summary: Savoury lentils and vegetables beneath a fluffy, golden mashed potato topping.
method: Simmer the peeled, cubed potatoes in salted water until easily pierced with a fork. Drain and mash with the butter, milk and salt until smooth.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Soften the onion and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook until their moisture has evaporated. Stir in the tomato paste and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the drained lentils and stock, then simmer uncovered until thick and spoonable. Season with salt and pepper and transfer to a baking dish.
Spread the mash over the filling and rough up the surface with a fork. Bake at 200°C until bubbling and lightly browned, then rest for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Make the potato topping
steps: Peel and cube potatoes, cover with cold salted water and simmer until easily pierced with a fork.
Drain thoroughly and mash with butter, milk and salt until smooth; set aside.

stages.title: Cook the vegetable base
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat and soften diced onion and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add chopped mushrooms and cook until their moisture has evaporated; stir in tomato paste and thyme for 1 minute.

stages.title: Simmer the filling
steps: Drain lentils and add with vegetable stock; simmer uncovered until thick and spoonable.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper; transfer to a baking dish.

stages.title: Top and bake
steps: Spread mashed potato over the lentils and rough up the surface with a fork to create crisp ridges.
Bake at 200°C until bubbling and lightly browned; rest 5 minutes before serving.

tips: The lentil filling should be thick before topping to avoid a watery pie.
variations: Add frozen peas to the filling during the last few minutes.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; freeze baked portions up to 3 months.

title: Greek chicken souvlaki
summary: Lemon-oregano chicken skewers served with warm pita, crisp salad and creamy tzatziki.
method: Cut the chicken into 3 cm pieces and toss with olive oil, juice of one lemon, two minced garlic cloves, oregano, paprika and salt. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, then skewer.
Grate the cucumber and squeeze out moisture. Stir into the yoghurt with the remaining garlic, a little lemon juice and salt, then chill.
Heat a grill pan or barbecue to medium-high and oil it. Cook the skewers for 10–12 minutes, turning, until charred and the chicken reaches 74°C.
Warm the pita and slice the tomatoes. Fill the pita with chicken, tomatoes, tzatziki and lemon wedges.

stages.title: Marinate the chicken
steps: Cut chicken into even 3 cm pieces and toss with olive oil, juice of one lemon, two minced garlic cloves, oregano, paprika and salt.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes if time allows; thread onto skewers just before cooking.

stages.title: Prepare tzatziki
steps: Grate cucumber, squeeze out moisture and stir into yoghurt with remaining garlic and a little lemon juice.
Season with salt and chill until serving.

stages.title: Grill the skewers
steps: Heat a grill pan or barbecue to medium-high for about 3 minutes, until hot, and lightly oil the surface.
Cook skewers for 10–12 minutes, turning regularly, until charred in spots and chicken reaches 74°C.

stages.title: Serve in pita
steps: Warm pita briefly and slice tomatoes.
Slide chicken from skewers into pita with tomatoes, tzatziki and lemon wedges.

tips: Chicken thigh stays juicy on high heat and tolerates slight charring.
variations: Use pork shoulder cubes, ensuring they are thoroughly cooked.
storage: Refrigerate cooked chicken up to 3 days; keep tzatziki separate.

title: Crispy tofu rice bowls
summary: Crispy tofu over rice with crunchy vegetables and a punchy sesame-soy dressing.
method: Cook the jasmine rice over low heat until tender, following the packet directions, and keep it covered.
Wrap the tofu in a clean towel and press under a plate for 10 minutes.
Cut the tofu into cubes, pat dry and toss with the cornflour and a pinch of salt.
Heat the neutral oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu until golden and crisp on several sides.
Whisk the soy sauce, maple syrup, rice vinegar and sesame oil. Slice the cucumber and julienne the carrots.
Divide the rice among bowls, add the vegetables and top with the tofu. Drizzle with the dressing just before eating.

stages.title: Cook rice and press tofu
steps: Cook rice according to packet instructions over low heat until tender and keep covered.
Wrap tofu in a clean towel and press under a plate for 10 minutes to remove excess moisture.

stages.title: Coat and crisp tofu
steps: Cut tofu into cubes, pat dry and toss lightly with cornflour and a pinch of salt.
Heat oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat and fry tofu, turning carefully, until golden and crisp on several sides.

stages.title: Mix the dressing
steps: Whisk soy sauce, maple syrup, vinegar and sesame oil together.
Slice cucumber and julienne carrots while tofu finishes cooking.

stages.title: Build the bowls
steps: Divide rice among bowls and add fresh vegetables.
Top with crisp tofu and drizzle dressing just before eating to preserve texture.

tips: Dry tofu thoroughly so the cornflour coating crisps.
variations: Add edamame or shredded red cabbage for extra vegetables.
storage: Refrigerate components separately up to 3 days; re-crisp tofu in a pan.

title: Spanish tortilla
summary: A thick Spanish potato and onion omelette with a golden exterior and tender centre.
method: Peel and thinly slice the potatoes and onion. Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper in a large bowl until just combined.
Heat the olive oil in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Cook the potatoes and onion gently until completely tender but not browned, then drain off most of the oil.
Fold the warm potato mixture into the eggs and rest for 3 minutes.
Cook in a lightly oiled nonstick pan over low heat until the edges set and the centre is mostly firm.
Invert onto a plate, slide back into the pan and cook until set through. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.

stages.title: Slice potatoes and onion
steps: Peel potatoes and slice into thin even rounds; thinly slice onion.
Beat eggs in a large bowl with salt and pepper until combined, without incorporating too much air.

stages.title: Gently cook potatoes
steps: Heat olive oil in a nonstick frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add potatoes and onion and cook gently, stirring occasionally, until completely tender but not browned; drain off most oil.

stages.title: Combine and set
steps: Fold warm potato mixture into eggs and rest 3 minutes.
Return to a lightly oiled nonstick pan over low heat and cook until edges set and centre is mostly firm.

stages.title: Flip and finish
steps: Place a flat plate over the pan and carefully invert the tortilla, using oven gloves.
Slide back into the pan and cook until set through; rest 5 minutes before slicing.

tips: Keep the heat low so potatoes soften without crisping.
variations: Add roasted peppers or a little parsley.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; serve chilled or reheat thoroughly.

title: Tuna and white bean salad
summary: Creamy white beans and flaky tuna tossed with lemon, parsley, red onion and olive oil.
ingredients: 2 cans tuna in olive oil (185 g each)
method: Drain, rinse and pat dry the cannellini beans. Halve the cherry tomatoes, dice the cucumber and slice the red onion as thinly as possible.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, Dijon mustard, salt and pepper until lightly emulsified. Taste and adjust the acidity.
Drain the tuna, flake it into large pieces and gently fold it through the beans and vegetables.
Add the dressing and parsley, tossing just enough to coat without crushing the beans.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Drain and rinse beans, then pat dry so dressing clings to them.
Halve tomatoes, dice cucumber and slice onion as thinly as possible.

stages.title: Mix the dressing
steps: Whisk lemon juice, olive oil, mustard, salt and pepper until lightly emulsified.
Taste and adjust acidity before adding to the salad.

stages.title: Combine and serve
steps: Flake drained tuna into large pieces and fold gently with beans and vegetables.
Add dressing and parsley, tossing just enough to coat without crushing beans.

tips: Use good-quality tuna packed in olive oil for richer flavour.
variations: Swap tuna for cooked chickpeas for a vegetarian salad.
storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days; keep dressing separate for best texture.

title: Roasted vegetable couscous
summary: Fluffy couscous with caramelised roast vegetables, fresh herbs and a lemony dressing.
method: Cut the courgette, red pepper, eggplant and red onion into bite-sized pieces. Toss with the olive oil, cumin and salt.
Roast at 210°C for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until caramelised at the edges.
Put the couscous and raisins in a heatproof bowl and pour over the boiling vegetable stock. Cover for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Fold the roasted vegetables through the couscous with the lemon zest and juice.
Scatter over the chopped mint and season to taste while warm.

stages.title: Roast the vegetables
steps: Cut courgette, pepper, eggplant and onion into even bite-sized pieces.
Toss with oil, cumin and salt and roast at 210°C for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until caramelised at the edges.

stages.title: Prepare couscous
steps: Place couscous and raisins in a heatproof bowl and pour over boiling vegetable stock.
Cover tightly for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork to separate grains.

stages.title: Finish the salad
steps: Fold roasted vegetables into couscous with lemon zest and juice.
Scatter chopped mint over the top and adjust seasoning while warm.

tips: Spread vegetables over two trays if needed to encourage roasting rather than steaming.
variations: Add crumbled feta or toasted almonds for extra richness.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; serve chilled or at room temperature after safe storage.

title: Turkey and avocado wraps
summary: Soft wraps packed with turkey, creamy avocado, crunchy greens and a tangy spread.
method: Mash the avocados with lemon juice and a pinch of salt. In a separate bowl, stir the Dijon mustard into the Greek yoghurt for the dressing.
Wash and dry the lettuce, slice the tomatoes and grate the carrot.
Spread the avocado over the centre of each tortilla, leaving a border. Layer on the lettuce, turkey, tomato and carrot, then drizzle with the dressing.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly from the bottom. Cut diagonally with a sharp knife and serve straight away.

stages.title: Mix the spread
steps: Mash avocado with lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Stir mustard into yoghurt in a separate bowl for a tangy dressing.

stages.title: Prepare fillings
steps: Wash and dry lettuce thoroughly, slice tomatoes and grate carrot.
Lay turkey slices out so they are ready to assemble quickly.

stages.title: Assemble wraps
steps: Spread avocado over the centre of each tortilla, leaving a border.
Layer lettuce, turkey, tomato and carrot, then drizzle with yoghurt dressing.

stages.title: Roll and serve
steps: Fold the sides inward and roll tightly from the bottom, keeping fillings tucked in.
Cut diagonally with a sharp knife and serve immediately.

tips: Dry vegetables well to stop tortillas becoming soggy.
variations: Use leftover roast chicken instead of turkey.
storage: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate assembled wraps up to 1 day.

title: Falafel pita pockets
summary: Golden falafel tucked into pita with crisp vegetables, pickles and creamy tahini sauce.
method: Drain and dry the chickpeas, then pulse with the onion, garlic, cumin, coriander and parsley until coarse, not smooth.
Stir in the flour and season with salt, then chill for 10 minutes.
Shape into 12 firm patties, adding a little more flour if the mixture is wet.
Heat the olive oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and cook the patties until golden on both sides and heated through.
Mix the yoghurt with finely diced cucumber and a pinch of salt. Warm the pita breads until warm through and slice open.
Stuff the pitas with falafel and cucumber yoghurt, adding lettuce or tomato if you like.

stages.title: Make the falafel mixture
steps: Drain and thoroughly dry chickpeas; pulse with onion, garlic, cumin, coriander and parsley until coarse, not smooth.
Stir in flour and season well; chill for 10 minutes to help the mixture hold together.

stages.title: Shape and cook
steps: Form 12 small patties, pressing firmly; add a little more flour if the mixture is wet.
Heat oil in a nonstick pan and cook patties over medium heat until golden on both sides and heated through.

stages.title: Prepare the sauce and fillings
steps: Mix yoghurt with finely diced cucumber and a pinch of salt.
Warm pita breads and slice pockets open carefully.

stages.title: Assemble
steps: Stuff pitas with falafel and cucumber yoghurt.
Add shredded lettuce or tomato if desired and serve immediately.

tips: Dry canned chickpeas well; wet mixture falls apart in the pan.
variations: Use a spoonful of tahini instead of yoghurt sauce.
storage: Refrigerate cooked falafel up to 3 days; reheat in oven to crisp.

title: Tomato and red pepper soup
summary: Velvety roasted tomato and red pepper soup with garlic, herbs and a gentle smoky sweetness.
method: Halve the tomatoes, deseed the red peppers and cut the onion into wedges. Toss on a tray with the unpeeled garlic and olive oil.
Roast at 210°C for about 25 minutes, until softened and lightly charred.
Squeeze the garlic from its skins and blend with the roasted vegetables, stock and smoked paprika until smooth, working in batches.
Pour into a saucepan and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes, until steaming hot.
Season with salt and pepper, then stir in the cream and torn basil just before serving.

stages.title: Roast the vegetables
steps: Halve tomatoes, deseed peppers and cut onion into wedges; arrange with unpeeled garlic on a tray.
Toss with olive oil and roast at 210°C until softened and lightly charred.

stages.title: Blend the soup
steps: Squeeze roasted garlic from its skins and transfer vegetables to a blender with stock and paprika.
Blend in batches, venting the lid carefully for hot liquid, until smooth.

stages.title: Simmer and finish
steps: Pour blended soup into a saucepan and simmer gently over low heat for 10 minutes, until steaming hot, to meld flavours.
Season with salt and pepper, then stir in cream and torn basil just before serving.

tips: Roasting concentrates sweetness without needing added sugar.
variations: Add a pinch of chilli flakes for heat.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; freeze without cream up to 3 months.

title: Egg and spinach breakfast muffins
summary: Portable egg muffins packed with spinach, vegetables and cheese, baked until just set.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C and lightly oil a 12-hole muffin tin with the olive oil.
Finely dice the red pepper and spring onions, and chop the baby spinach.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper until just combined, then stir in the vegetables and grated cheddar.
Divide the mixture between the muffin holes, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 16–20 minutes until puffed and fully set in the centre.
Rest in the tin for 5 minutes, then loosen the edges and serve warm.

stages.title: Prepare vegetables
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C and lightly oil a 12-hole muffin tin with the olive oil.
Finely dice red pepper and spring onions; chop spinach so it distributes evenly.

stages.title: Mix the eggs
steps: Whisk eggs with milk, salt and pepper until just combined.
Stir in vegetables and grated cheddar without overbeating.

stages.title: Bake the muffins
steps: Divide mixture between muffin holes, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 16–20 minutes until puffed and fully set in the centre.

stages.title: Cool and remove
steps: Let muffins stand in the tin for 5 minutes; they will settle slightly as they cool.
Loosen edges with a silicone spatula and serve warm.

tips: Grease the tin thoroughly to prevent sticking.
variations: Add diced cooked mushrooms or cooked ham.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freeze individually up to 2 months.

title: French toast with cinnamon
summary: Thick slices of bread soaked in cinnamon custard and pan-fried until golden and soft inside.
method: Whisk the eggs, milk, vanilla and cinnamon in a shallow dish until fully blended.
Heat a large nonstick frying pan over medium heat and melt a little butter.
Dip each brioche slice briefly in the custard on both sides, then let the excess drip off.
Cook the slices in batches, 2–3 minutes per side until golden and set in the centre. Add butter as needed and lower the heat if they brown too fast.
Stack on warm plates, scatter over the sliced strawberries, drizzle with maple syrup and serve immediately.

stages.title: Make the custard
steps: Whisk eggs, milk, vanilla and cinnamon in a shallow dish until fully blended.
Set a large nonstick frying pan over medium heat and melt a little butter.

stages.title: Soak the bread
steps: Dip each brioche slice briefly into custard on both sides, allowing it to absorb without falling apart.
Let excess custard drip back into the dish before cooking.

stages.title: Cook in batches
steps: Lay slices in the pan without crowding and cook for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and set in the centre.
Add more butter between batches as needed, lowering heat if the brioche browns too fast.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Stack slices on warm plates and scatter sliced strawberries over them.
Drizzle with maple syrup and serve immediately.

tips: Day-old brioche absorbs custard without becoming mushy.
variations: Use sourdough for a less sweet version.
storage: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate cooked slices up to 2 days and reheat in a pan.

title: Banana oat pancakes
summary: Naturally sweet banana and oat pancakes with tender centres and lightly golden edges.
method: Blend the bananas, eggs, oats, milk, baking powder, cinnamon and vanilla until mostly smooth.
Rest the batter for 5 minutes so it thickens slightly.
Warm a nonstick frying pan over medium-low heat and grease lightly with the butter. Test a teaspoon of batter to check it cooks gently without scorching.
Spoon small rounds into the pan, leaving room to flip. Cook 2–3 minutes until the edges look set, then flip and cook another 1–2 minutes.
Stack the pancakes and serve with yoghurt if you like. Loosen any leftover batter with a splash of milk if it thickens.

stages.title: Blend the batter
steps: Blend bananas, eggs, oats, milk, baking powder, cinnamon and vanilla until mostly smooth.
Let batter stand for 5 minutes so oats hydrate and it thickens slightly.

stages.title: Heat the pan
steps: Warm a nonstick frying pan over medium-low heat and lightly grease with butter.
Drop a teaspoon of batter to test that it cooks gently without scorching.

stages.title: Cook pancakes
steps: Spoon small rounds of batter into the pan, leaving space to flip.
Cook 2–3 minutes until edges look set, then turn carefully and cook another 1–2 minutes.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Stack pancakes and serve with fruit or a little yoghurt.
Add a splash of milk to remaining batter if it thickens too much.

tips: Keep pancakes small because oat batter is delicate.
variations: Add blueberries or a pinch of nutmeg.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freeze separated with baking paper up to 2 months.

title: Baked oatmeal with apple
summary: Warm baked oats with tender apple, cinnamon and a lightly golden, comforting top.
method: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a medium baking dish with the butter. Dice the apples and roughly chop the walnuts.
Whisk the eggs, milk, maple syrup and vanilla in a large bowl. Stir in the oats, baking powder, cinnamon and apples.
Pour into the dish and scatter with walnuts. Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the centre is set and the top is lightly golden.
Rest for 5 minutes so it holds its shape, then serve warm with yoghurt (optional) or a splash of milk.

stages.title: Prepare the dish
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C and grease a medium baking dish with butter.
Core and dice apples into small pieces; roughly chop walnuts.

stages.title: Mix wet and dry ingredients
steps: Whisk eggs, milk, maple syrup and vanilla in a large bowl.
Stir in oats, baking powder, cinnamon and apples until evenly combined.

stages.title: Bake
steps: Pour mixture into prepared dish and scatter walnuts on top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until centre is set and surface lightly golden.

stages.title: Rest and portion
steps: Let baked oats stand for 5 minutes so slices hold their shape.
Serve warm with yoghurt or a splash of milk.

tips: Use rolled oats for texture; instant oats become soft and pasty.
variations: Swap apples for pears and walnuts for pecans.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; freeze individual squares up to 2 months.

title: Breakfast hash with potatoes
summary: Crispy pan-fried potatoes with peppers, onions and eggs for a hearty breakfast skillet.
method: Dice the potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes and simmer in salted water for about 8 minutes until just tender at the edges. Drain and let the steam escape for 2 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Spread the potatoes in one layer and cook undisturbed until golden, then season with the smoked paprika and garlic powder.
Add the diced onion and red pepper and cook until softened and lightly charred. Season with salt, keeping the potatoes crisp.
Make four spaces in the hash and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook until the whites are set.
Sprinkle with the parsley and serve straight from the pan.

stages.title: Parboil potatoes
steps: Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes and simmer in salted water until just tender at the edges.
Drain thoroughly and allow steam to evaporate for 2 minutes so they crisp in the pan.

stages.title: Crisp the potatoes
steps: Heat oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and spread potatoes in one layer.
Cook without stirring for several minutes at a time until golden; season with paprika and garlic powder.

stages.title: Add vegetables
steps: Add diced onion and pepper and cook until softened and lightly charred.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper, keeping the potatoes crisp.

stages.title: Cook eggs and serve
steps: Make four spaces in the hash and crack in eggs, then cover briefly until whites set.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve straight from the pan.

tips: Dry potatoes thoroughly after boiling for crisp edges.
variations: Add cooked sausage or sautéed mushrooms.
storage: Refrigerate hash without eggs up to 3 days; cook eggs fresh.

title: Garlic green beans with almonds
summary: Tender green beans tossed with garlic butter and toasted almonds for a crisp, nutty side.
method: Boil the trimmed green beans in salted water for 3–4 minutes until bright green and just tender. Cool in cold water, then dry well.
Toast the flaked almonds in a dry frying pan over medium heat, shaking often, until lightly golden. Tip onto a plate straight away.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in the pan over medium heat. Add the finely sliced garlic and cook for 20–30 seconds.
Toss in the beans until hot. Add the lemon juice, almonds and a little black pepper.

stages.title: Blanch the beans
steps: Trim bean ends and cook in boiling salted water for 3–4 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Drain and plunge into cold water briefly to stop cooking, then dry well.

stages.title: Toast almonds
steps: Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat and toast flaked almonds, shaking often, until lightly golden.
Transfer immediately to a plate to prevent burning.

stages.title: Sauté and finish
steps: Melt butter with olive oil, add finely sliced garlic and cook for 20–30 seconds.
Toss in beans until hot, then add lemon juice, almonds and a little black pepper.

tips: Dry beans before sautéing to avoid splattering and dilution.
variations: Use toasted hazelnuts instead of almonds.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat briefly in a pan.

title: Honey roasted carrots
summary: Roasted carrots caramelised with honey, olive oil and herbs until sweet and tender.
method: Preheat the oven to 210°C and line a baking tray. Peel the carrots if needed and halve any thick ones lengthwise so they cook evenly.
Toss the carrots with the olive oil, thyme and salt, then spread in a single layer on the tray.
Roast for 20–25 minutes, turning once, until the edges start to caramelise.
Drizzle over the honey, toss to coat, then roast 5 more minutes until glossy and golden, watching so they don't burn. Finish with the lemon juice.

stages.title: Prepare the carrots
steps: Preheat oven to 210°C and line a baking tray.
Peel carrots if needed and cut thick ones lengthwise so pieces cook evenly.

stages.title: Roast until tender
steps: Toss carrots with oil, thyme and salt and spread in a single layer.
Roast for 20–25 minutes, turning once, until edges begin to caramelise.

stages.title: Glaze and finish
steps: Drizzle honey over carrots and toss carefully to coat.
Return to oven for 5 minutes, watching closely to prevent burning; finish with lemon juice.

tips: Add honey near the end because it burns at high heat.
variations: Use maple syrup instead of honey for a vegan version.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat in the oven.

title: Creamy coleslaw
summary: Shredded cabbage and carrot in a creamy, tangy dressing with a satisfying crunch.
method: Core and finely shred the white and red cabbage, then grate the carrots and pat the vegetables dry of excess moisture.
Whisk the mayonnaise, Greek yoghurt, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard and sugar until smooth.
Season the dressing with salt and pepper, tasting until the tang and sweetness are balanced.
Toss the vegetables with the dressing until evenly coated.
Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes, then give it a final stir just before serving.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Remove tough cabbage cores and shred both cabbages finely with a sharp knife or mandoline.
Grate carrots and pat any excess moisture from vegetables.

stages.title: Mix the dressing
steps: Whisk mayonnaise, yoghurt, vinegar, mustard and sugar until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper and taste for a balance of acidity and sweetness.

stages.title: Toss and chill
steps: Combine vegetables with dressing and toss until evenly coated.
Refrigerate for at least 15 minutes before serving, stirring once more just beforehand.

tips: Dress just before serving if you prefer a very crisp slaw.
variations: Use all yoghurt instead of mayonnaise for a lighter dressing.
storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days; do not freeze.

title: Crispy smashed potatoes
summary: Boiled potatoes smashed and roasted until deeply crisp, with fluffy middles and savoury seasoning.
method: Cover the baby potatoes with cold salted water, bring to the boil, then simmer until a knife slides in easily.
Drain and let them steam dry for 5 minutes.
Space the potatoes out on an oiled baking tray and flatten each gently with the base of a glass.
Brush with olive oil and sprinkle over the rosemary, minced garlic and flaky salt.
Roast at 220°C for 20–25 minutes until deep golden and crisp, adding the parmesan for the last 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Rest for 2 minutes to firm the crisp edges, then serve with yoghurt if you like.

stages.title: Boil potatoes
steps: Place whole baby potatoes in salted cold water, bring to a boil and simmer until a knife slides in easily.
Drain and allow to steam dry for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Smash and season
steps: Arrange potatoes on an oiled baking tray with space between them.
Flatten each gently with the base of a glass, then brush with oil and sprinkle with rosemary, minced garlic and salt.

stages.title: Roast until crisp
steps: Roast at 220°C for 20–25 minutes until edges are deep golden and crisp.
Sprinkle with parmesan for the last 5 minutes so it melts and browns lightly.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Let potatoes rest for 2 minutes to firm their crisp edges.
Serve immediately with yoghurt dip or aioli.

tips: Steam drying is essential for a crisp surface.
variations: Use smoked paprika instead of rosemary.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat in a hot oven or air fryer.

title: Sesame cucumber salad
summary: Cool, crunchy cucumber tossed in a tangy sesame-soy dressing with chilli and garlic.
method: Slice the cucumbers into thin rounds, or lightly crush and cut into chunks. Toss with the salt and rest for 10 minutes.
Drain the cucumbers and pat them dry.
Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, honey and chilli flakes until combined. Taste and adjust the vinegar or sweetness.
Just before serving, coat the cucumbers with the dressing, scatter over the sesame seeds and serve chilled.

stages.title: Salt the cucumber
steps: Slice cucumbers into thin rounds or lightly crush and cut into chunks.
Toss with salt and rest 10 minutes to draw out excess moisture; drain and pat dry.

stages.title: Mix the dressing
steps: Whisk rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, honey and chilli flakes until combined.
Taste and adjust vinegar or sweetness to your preference.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Coat cucumbers with dressing just before serving.
Scatter sesame seeds over the top and serve chilled.

tips: Salting prevents the dressing from becoming watery.
variations: Add thinly sliced spring onions or fresh coriander.
storage: Refrigerate up to 1 day; best eaten soon after dressing.

title: Cornbread with honey butter
summary: Tender golden cornbread with a lightly crisp crust, served with sweet honey butter.
method: Preheat the oven to 200°C and grease a 20 cm square tin. Whisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt in one bowl.
Beat the eggs, buttermilk, melted butter and 1 tbsp honey in another bowl.
Fold the wet mix into the dry until no dry flour remains. A few small lumps are fine.
Spread the batter in the tin and bake 20–25 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.
Beat the softened butter with the remaining honey and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Cut the cornbread into squares and serve warm with a little honey butter on each.

stages.title: Prepare the batter
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C and grease a 20 cm square baking tin.
Whisk cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt in one bowl; beat eggs, buttermilk, melted butter and 1 tbsp honey in another.

stages.title: Combine gently
steps: Pour wet ingredients into dry and fold just until no dry flour remains.
Do not overmix; a few small lumps are fine.

stages.title: Bake
steps: Spread batter in the tin and bake for 20–25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes before cutting.

stages.title: Make honey butter
steps: Beat softened butter with remaining honey and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Serve a little over each warm square.

tips: Overmixing develops gluten and makes cornbread tough.
variations: Add chopped jalapeños and cheddar for a savoury version.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; freeze slices up to 2 months.

title: Roasted cauliflower with tahini
summary: Caramelised cauliflower florets drizzled with lemony tahini and finished with fresh herbs.
method: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Cut the cauliflower into evenly sized florets, dry well and toss with the olive oil, cumin, paprika and salt.
Spread the florets on a baking tray, cut sides down where possible. Roast for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until tender and browned at the edges.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice, grated garlic and a pinch of salt. Add the cold water gradually until smooth and pourable.
Transfer the hot cauliflower to a platter and drizzle with the tahini dressing. Finish with the parsley and extra lemon wedges.

stages.title: Prepare cauliflower
steps: Preheat oven to 220°C and cut cauliflower into medium florets of similar size.
Dry well and toss with olive oil, cumin, paprika and salt.

stages.title: Roast until golden
steps: Spread florets in a single layer on a baking tray, cut sides down where possible.
Roast 25–30 minutes, turning once, until tender and browned at the edges.

stages.title: Make tahini dressing
steps: Whisk tahini with lemon juice, grated garlic and a pinch of salt.
Add cold water gradually until the dressing becomes smooth and pourable.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Transfer hot cauliflower to a platter and drizzle with tahini dressing.
Finish with parsley and extra lemon wedges.

tips: Leave space between florets for caramelisation.
variations: Add toasted pine nuts or pomegranate seeds.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; store dressing separately.

title: Garlic butter mushrooms
summary: Golden sautéed mushrooms coated in garlic butter, herbs and their own savoury juices.
method: Brush the mushrooms clean (or rinse quickly and dry well) and halve any large ones so the pieces are a similar size.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave for 2–3 minutes.
Turn the mushrooms and cook until the moisture has evaporated and they are browned.
Lower the heat to medium-low. Add the butter and minced garlic and toss for 30–60 seconds until fragrant.
Finish with the lemon juice, parsley, salt and black pepper, then serve.

stages.title: Prepare mushrooms
steps: Brush mushrooms clean or rinse quickly and dry thoroughly.
Halve large mushrooms so all pieces are similar in size.

stages.title: Brown mushrooms
steps: Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add mushrooms in a single layer and leave undisturbed for 2–3 minutes before turning; cook until moisture evaporates.

stages.title: Add butter and aromatics
steps: Lower heat and add butter and minced garlic, tossing for 30–60 seconds until fragrant.
Finish with lemon juice, parsley, salt and black pepper.

tips: Use a wide pan and cook in batches to avoid steaming.
variations: Add a splash of white wine before the butter and reduce fully.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat in a hot pan.

title: Vanilla panna cotta
summary: Silky vanilla cream set into a delicate dessert and served with bright fruit sauce.
method: Soak the gelatine leaves in cold water for 5 minutes until soft.
Split the vanilla bean and scrape the seeds into a saucepan with the cream, milk and sugar. Warm over low heat until the sugar dissolves, without boiling.
Off the heat, squeeze the water from the gelatine and whisk it in until fully dissolved.
Strain through a fine sieve into six ramekins, cool slightly, then cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until softly set.
Dip the bases briefly in warm water and turn out onto plates, or serve in the ramekins. Top with the berries just before serving.

stages.title: Bloom gelatine
steps: Soak gelatine leaves in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes until soft.
Meanwhile split the vanilla bean and scrape seeds into a saucepan with cream, milk and sugar.

stages.title: Heat the cream
steps: Warm cream mixture gently, stirring until sugar dissolves; do not let it boil.
Remove from heat, squeeze excess water from gelatine and whisk it into the hot mixture until fully dissolved.

stages.title: Set in moulds
steps: Strain mixture through a fine sieve and divide between six small ramekins.
Cool slightly, cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours until softly set.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Dip mould bases briefly in warm water and invert onto plates, or serve directly in ramekins.
Top with berries just before serving.

tips: Avoid boiling after adding gelatine; a gentle set is the goal.
variations: Infuse with orange zest instead of vanilla.
storage: Refrigerate covered up to 3 days; do not freeze.

title: Tiramisu
summary: Coffee-soaked sponge layered with airy mascarpone cream and a dusting of cocoa.
method: Whip the cold cream with the sugar and vanilla to soft peaks, then gently fold in the mascarpone until smooth and thick.
Pour the cooled coffee into a shallow bowl and briefly dip each savoiardi biscuit on both sides, so they stay firm and don't go soggy.
Arrange a single layer of dipped biscuits in a dish and spread over half the mascarpone cream.
Repeat with the remaining biscuits and cream, then smooth the top.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight, until set.
Dust generously with the cocoa powder just before serving.

stages.title: Make the cream
steps: Whip cold cream with sugar and vanilla to soft peaks.
Fold mascarpone into whipped cream gently until smooth and thick; avoid overmixing.

stages.title: Prepare the biscuits
steps: Pour cooled coffee into a shallow bowl.
Dip each savoiardi biscuit briefly on both sides; do not soak or the dessert will become soggy.

stages.title: Layer the dessert
steps: Arrange a single layer of dipped biscuits in a dish and spread over half the mascarpone cream.
Repeat with remaining biscuits and cream, smoothing the top with a spatula.

stages.title: Chill and finish
steps: Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, to set and meld flavours.
Dust generously with cocoa just before serving.

tips: Use fully cooled coffee to keep the cream stable.
variations: Add a little grated dark chocolate between layers.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; keep chilled and do not leave at room temperature.
